## Packages

```{r}
library('dplyr')
library('ggplot2')
```


## Datasets

The chosen data set to be studied was "US Groceries and Gas Prices (2015-2026) \\
We decided that the data set is relevant to the current social/political
issues that US citizens are confronting. High prices. \\

```{r}
avg_item_summary <- read.csv(file.choose(),header=T) #avg $ item summary
avg_price_monthly <- read.csv(file.choose(),header=T) #avg $ monthly
avg_price_wide <- read.csv(file.choose(),header=T) #avg $ wide
```

## Analysis 1

Firstly getting the number of observations and then the number of columns in our data set.
```{r}
nrow(avg_item_summary)
ncol(avg_item_summary)
```

```{r}
summary(avg_item_summary)
```
